title: Final Learning Experiences Presentation
text:
KENYA INSTITUTE OF CURRICULUM DEVELOPMENT
 OBJECTIVES
By the end of the Session participants should be able to:
1) Define learning experiences
2) Discuss the importance of learning outcomes
3) Discuss factors necessary in selection of learning experiences
4) Discuss types of learning experiences in the curriculum designs
5) Appreciate the role parents and learning experiences play in
 education.
 Activity 1:
• Lead the participants in the plenary to discuss when
 learning takes place.
• How can they define learning.
• What are learning experiences?
 INTRODUCTION
• Learning refers to the relative permanent change in behaviour
 brought about through interactions or experiences with the
 environment.
• Learning Experiences can be defined as interaction in which learning
 takes place.
• A learner is exposed to situations and activities so as to develop
 desired knowledge, skills, values and attitudes.
• The experiences could be:
 Formal featuring the classroom conditions and teaching methods;
 Non-formal during which the learner is engaged in organized and
 structured activities taking place in or outside school
 Informal which entails general school and home social interactions.
• Tyler defines LE as “the interaction between the learner and external
 conditions in the environment to which he/she can react.”
 Contd…
• It covers how, when and where learning takes
 place
• Teacher has the responsibility to invoke the
 experience in which learning takes place.
• Selecting LE is guided by certain principles

 Activity 3:
•Ask participants in groups of 3-5 to
 discuss the purpose of learning
 experiences and the factors to
 consider when selecting activities
 for their learners?
 Purpose of Learning Experiences
Learning experiences enable the learner to:
• acquire knowledge and develop skills, values and attitudes
• acquire the intended core competencies
• self-regulate and evaluate
• engage deeply in the learnt concepts
• reflect on the learning process
• interact with others during the learning process.
 Factors to consider when selecting learning
 experiences
•Relevance to intended learning outcomes
•Developmental age level
•Learning resources
•Safety
•Size of the class
•Time required for the experience
Activity 3
• Provide participants with excerpts of curriculum designs in an activity
 area.
• In pairs, ask them to identify the types of learning experiences
 provided in the curriculum design
• Let them discuss the differences/similarities among the learning
 experiences
LEARNING EXPERIENCES IN CURRICULUM
DESIGNS
The Curriculum Design has provided for LEs as:
• Suggested Learning Experiences as per sub-strand
• Non- formal learning experiences
• Community Service Learning Activities
• Linkage activities to PCIs
 What Informs Learning Experiences
In Competency Based Curriculum, learner should be given
opportunities to take responsibility for their learning through:
embracing:
 Differentiated learning
 Multiple Intelligence Theory
 Learning Styles
 Differentiated Learning
Learning Approach based on the fact that students differ in
their:
• Learning styles
• Needs and interests
• Strengths and abilities
• Learning pace
Classroom activities should be adapted to meet these
differences.
Teachers Can Differentiate
Content Process Product Environment
 According to Students’
 Learning
 Readiness Interest
 Profile
 Adapted from The Differentiated Classroom: Responding to the Needs of All Learners (Tomlinson, 1999).
 DL Contd…
• Differentiated learning recognizes that learners
 learn differently and benefit from differentiated
 learning techniques in the classroom. It shifts
 focus from the “one-size-fits-all” approach to
 learning. The teacher, therefore, should employ
 varied learning experiences to cater for the
 different learning styles among learners.
 Ultimately, this will lead to improved learning
 outcomes.
 Multiple Intelligences Theory
•Dr Howard Gardner posits through
 research that individuals possess
 multiple intelligences that should be
 identified and nurtured as indicated in
 the following:
 Learning Styles
• There are four broad learning styles have been identified.
 These are Visual (Seeing), Aural(Hearing), Kinesthetic
 (Doing) Reading and Writing.
• Some learners tend to learn best through one of the four, but
 supported by the other three, (refer to Figure).
• The teacher needs to ensure that all learners are catered for
 in each lesson by providing varied experiences.

 Principles of Good LEs
• Validity: To achieve given learning outcomes learners
 must be given opportunities to practise the specific
 behaviour indicated in the learning outcome.
 If focus is to solve problems in sanitation, ample
 opportunities should be provided for learners to come
 into contact with real problems and find solutions.
 Principles Contd…
• Variety: Use of varied experiences (multisensory) to
 achieve the same learning outcome so long as they
 meet the criteria for effective learning
• Comprehensiveness: all the learning outcomes have
 corresponding LEs
• Adds value to the learner: LE puts learner first and
 should be purposeful
Contd….
• Promotes further learning: inspires pupils and
 students to be long-life learners
• Effective: Should enrich learning and not substitute it
• The learner must obtain satisfaction from carrying the
 kind of behaviour implied by the learning outcome.
 e.g. if the learning outcome focuses on developing
 reading skills the learner must read widely
Suggested Learning Experiences
• The suggested learning experiences cover:
 Knowledge
 Skills
 Values
 Attitudes
 • They are related to the content, specific learning
 outcomes and learning resources, are varied and
 include use of ICT devices

Examples of Tasks/Activities
 Non-formal learning experiences
• Non-Formal learning experiences refers to any organized, structured
 and systematic learning activities, which supplement and support
 acquisition of the and application of knowledge, skills, attitudes and
 values as envisaged in the competency-based curriculum.
• They are structured learning activities that are geared towards
 development of affective and psychomotor dimensions of learning.
 Some of the non-formal activities may include: singing, dancing,
 reciting poems, clubs and societies’ activities, cultural festivals, music
 and drama festivals, science fairs, games and debates
 Community Service Learning experiences
• These are learning experiences where learners
 are given opportunities to apply the acquired
 knowledge and skills to solve an identified
 problem within the community while at the
 same time improving own learning outcomes.
• e.g. Learners identify struggling readers in the
 family/neighbourhood and teach them how to
 read
Pertinent and Contemporary Issues
• Activity 6: Participants discuss what they understand by PCIs
 and identify the PCIs prevalent in their region
 PCIs Contd…
• PCIs should be identified from the curriculum design.
• They are mainstreamed in all the Learning Areas and, in the
 schemes of work and lesson plans under the learning
 experiences.
• The teacher is expected to make conscious and deliberate
 efforts to bring PCIs out during the learning experiences
 failure to which he/she will unintentionally simply focus on
 the subject matter without give due consideration to them.
 Why PCIs?
• Mainstreaming PCI as a learning experience provides the
 learner with the opportunity be aware of the issues and
 challenges facing people in the society.
• During the learning experiences be it formally, non-
 formerly or in formerly, those issues are discussed
 relating them with real life situations/circumstances.
• During the learning experiences, learners are given an
 opportunity to develop and apply both cognitive and
 psychosocial competencies that enable them to deal with
 realities and challenges of everyday life.
 Examples of how PCIs are mainstreamed in
 the Curriculum Designs.
The following are examples of PCIs in selected Learning Areas
• Movement Activities
• Grade: 1
• Strand: Basic motor skills
• Sub strand: Locomotor skills; Jumping for height
• The PCIs being focused on is HIV and AIDS under Health Related Issues.
• The teacher advices the learners to report to him/her should one of them
 gets hurt ( wounds and cuts occur) while playing games instead of handling
 them.

The role of parents in the learning process of a
 child.
• There is great recognition that Parents play a
 pivotal role in determining the success of a child’s
 education.
• They are expected to be the first and best nurturers,
 stimulators and educators of their children.
• They have a shared responsibility with schools to
 provide an enabling environment that is conducive
 to learning and which motivates the child to achieve
 their full potential.
 PEE Contd…
Activity 8:In groups of three, brainstorm on why it is
important to involve a parent/guardian in the
learning process of the child in CBC?
• Parents should be empowered and engaged in
 the learning process of the child because:
• Learning goes beyond the 4 walls of a classroom.
 Learning experiences should be extended at home
 to, reinforce what was learnt in school .
 PEE Contd…
• Home should provide a platform for the learner to
 practise what was learnt in school
• The new dimension in learning focus on the learner
 as opposed to teaching. Learning should continue
 wherever the learner is .
• A learner is a natural explorer and the parents
 should therefore provide moral support, resources
 required for stimulation, exploration and
 development of competencies.
 PEE Contd…
• Parents need to know that the focus is more on formative
 as opposed to summative assessment.
• Learners will not be competing against each other but
 against themselves so as to reach their highest potential.
• They should support learners in identification and
 nurturing of talents and in determining the learners
 career identification and progression
• KICD has developed PE&E Framework which will provide
 further guidance on how schools can empower parents to
 contribute to the learning outcomes of their children and
 to be engaged at all levels of Basic Education.
PEE Contd….
• Empowerment refers process of strengthening the
 capacity of parents to be actively engaged in nurturing
 learners’ potential in and out of school. (increase
 knowledge, skills, change attitudes and practices)
• Parental engagement is about all activities that parents
 undertake to help their children succeed in school and life.
 It is a shared and continuous responsibility for parents in
 the child’s education
• School management and teachers should be
 encouraged to utilize the guidelines to empower and
 engage the parents so that the schools and parents are
 jointly involved in nurturing learners potential.
Summary
 Quote 2
“Parents are the ultimate role models for
children. Every word, movement, action
has an effect. No other person or outside
force has influence over the child than
the parent.”
